Executive structural synthesis

Croatia's quarterly national-accounts picture is classified as cautious / mixed with structural pressure. Growth Quality: Broad-based growth. Investment Quality: Construction-heavy. Competitiveness: Productivity gains with labour-cost pressure. Household Demand: Mixed household demand. External Sector: External drag on growth. Across the five modules, 1 are favourable, 2 mixed/neutral and 2 adverse.

Investment structure & quality

The fixed-investment mix in 2026-Q2 is classified as construction-heavy. GFCF stood at 25.4% of GDP versus 21.5% for EU-27. Machinery/equipment plus intellectual property accounted for 41.8% of GFCF, while construction accounted for 58.2%. Total real GFCF growth was +1.7% year-on-year in 2026-Q2.

Productivity, labour cost & competitiveness

The current structural signal is classified as productivity gains with labour-cost pressure. On the latest common comparison quarter (2026-Q2), real labour productivity per hour grew +1.3% year-on-year versus +0.8% in EU-27. Nominal unit labour cost per hour increased +7.5% versus +2.8% in EU-27. Watchpoints: Elevated NULC growth; Large NULC gap versus EU.

Household demand & consumption mix

The current household-demand mix is classified as mixed household demand. Real household consumption grew +0.8% year-on-year in 2026-Q2. Durables accounted for 5.6% of nominal household expenditure and services for 49.1% in 2026-Q2.

External sector & trade contribution

The external-sector contribution is classified as external drag on growth. Net exports contributed -0.38 percentage points to GDP growth in 2026-Q2. Exports contributed +1.53 pp and imports -1.91 pp. Real exports grew +3.2% YoY while real imports grew +3.6% YoY. Watchpoints: Domestic demand accompanied by import drag.

Methodology and interpretation

The growth-regime, growth-balance and watchpoint labels are transparent A-CLUSTER analytical rules. They are not Eurostat classifications. The report chooses the latest quarter with headline real GDP growth and a sufficiently populated expenditure decomposition. Structural indicators such as productivity, unit labour costs and GFCF may have different release lags; their observation quarter is disclosed explicitly. The household durability module (namq_10_fcs) follows the domestic consumption concept and is not identical to the household/NPISH aggregate used in the GDP expenditure decomposition. A reconciliation residual larger than ±0.35 percentage points is flagged rather than silently treated as a complete decomposition.
Data source: Eurostat datasets namq_10_gdp, namq_10_lp_ulc, namq_10_an6 and namq_10_fcs.
